00: The existing wizard supplies the server, secret, identity and contract setup steps. This welcome screen is new, not a separate account or profile system.
Offer setup and the advanced editor as entry points. Explain that credentials come from the network administrator. Do not imply that PHPVPN provides a hosted VPN subscription.
The setup link opens the prefilled URL sample. No configuration file is inspected on launch.
01: Show Connected only for a confirmed connected state. Duration and traffic counters come from the client status. Opening connection details must not start a new connection.
Keep Disconnect prominent and route the four bottom destinations consistently. Describe access to the virtual network, not guaranteed protection for all internet traffic.
The duration and counters are fixed examples. Other pages are independent states, so navigating away does not preserve a simulated live connection.
02: Connect uses the current configuration. The server and credentials are checked during connection, so a stored configuration is not proof that the server is currently reachable.
Before starting a real Android connection, request system VPN consent when required. If consent is already available, skip the illustrative permission screen.
Connect always opens the consent example. This does not mean Android should ask on every connection.
03: The desktop connection flow has no Android permission dialog. This is an additional platform step, not server authentication.
Use the system-owned VPN consent flow. Cancellation must not be shown as a server error or as a successful connection. Android controls the actual wording and appearance.
Allow and Cancel only navigate to prepared pages. The HTML dialog cannot grant system permission.
04: The existing progress UI distinguishes URL, server secret, access key and communication contract checks. A failed or unavailable check must not be displayed as successful.
Use clear text as well as status colors. Continue to expose cancellation while connecting. Move to Connected only after confirmation, not merely after the last local animation.
There is no automatic timer. Use the scenario selector to inspect success, failure or cancellation. Cancel opens the disconnecting sample.
05: The runtime distinguishes reconnecting from connected. Recovery does not by itself confirm that the virtual network is available.
Explain that recovery is in progress and keep the disconnect action available. Do not promise a kill switch or blocking of non-VPN traffic, neither of which is established by this design.
The sample does not retry a network request. Success and failure are separate scenario pages, and no retry interval is specified.
06: Transport failure and input validation are separate. A timeout is not evidence of a wrong secret. HTTP error details are available only if diagnostic data was captured.
Explain the failure and provide a retry or a relevant configuration route. Hide the HTTP details action when no such data exists in a real result.
The timeout screen links to an independent sample HTTP 503 response. These are illustrative states, not one captured request. No real diagnostics are collected.
07: Disconnection remains pending until the service confirms the result. A timeout can lead to Disconnect not confirmed rather than a success state.
Keep the progress state distinct from Disconnected. Do not dismiss uncertainty just because the screen is closed or the app is backgrounded.
The disabled action indicates a pending example. Select the confirmed or unknown result in the scenario selector. No service is stopped.
08: Unavailable status cannot establish whether the VPN is connected or disconnected. Previously received statistics may be retained with a stale-data notice.
State the uncertainty explicitly and distinguish the last known state from current status. A new status read should lead to whichever state is actually confirmed.
Check status again links to a connecting example. That link is not a rule that an unknown state should trigger a fresh connection.
09: The desktop tray provides access to connection controls. The Android notification is a proposed platform replacement, not an existing desktop screen.

An active service notification should open the app status and offer an appropriate disconnect action. Remove it when the service becomes inactive. Do not equate closing the activity with stopping VPN.
This is an HTML representation, not a system notification. Layout and available controls can vary with Android. Always-on behavior is outside this concept.
10: The hub maps the existing wizard, contracts, configuration editor, server information, statistics, About and Exit capabilities. Advanced parameters remain available in JSON.
Keep frequent destinations in bottom navigation and configuration tasks in Settings. Do not invent profile switching, country selection or account management.
The wizard link demonstrates the active-connection gate. A real disconnected session should go directly to setup. This page does not read live connection status.
11: The wizard disconnectGate prevents setup checks from proceeding until VPN disconnection is known. An already disconnected client can proceed without disconnecting again.
Explain the interruption before the action. Proceed to URL setup only after confirmed disconnection. Preserve an exit route that leaves the existing connection in place.
Disconnect and continue opens the URL sample immediately. The intermediate wait is omitted here, but the unknown outcome is available as a scenario.
12: A server URL supports HTTP or HTTPS and must not contain user information, a query or a fragment. The wizard verifies the endpoint before the next authentication step. Finish performs the eventual save.
Keep URL input and optional HTTP headers separate. Distinguish a malformed URL from a transport timeout. Do not mark a valid URL syntactically invalid just because the network is unavailable.
Verify opens a prepared successful result regardless of typed input. The URL is a sample and is never contacted.
13: The headers editor belongs to the wizard draft and offers accept, reset and cancel. Cancel preserves the previously accepted value rather than committing the current edit.
Use multiline editing with one header per line. Preserve the full value without silently truncating long headers. Treat possible sensitive header content accordingly.
Reset loads an illustrative header value, not a guaranteed copy of the service defaults. Use in wizard does not transfer text between these independent HTML pages.
14: The wizard supports a custom server secret or the default secret. Selecting the default disables custom entry. A predictable default is distinct from a private administrator-provided secret.
Hide sensitive input initially and let the user reveal it deliberately. Do not repeat the secret in an error message. Advance only after the actual verification succeeds.
The default switch disables the field and Show/Hide works locally. Verify navigates to the next prepared page without performing authentication.
15: The identity step supports a virtual IP, automatic IP suggestion and a custom or default access key. When no suggestion is available, the user can enter an administrator-assigned address.

Keep IP and access key distinct from the server secret. Disable the corresponding manual input when its automatic/default option is selected. Do not claim that a suggested address has been verified before the check completes.
The IP and key are samples. Toggling automatic IP only enables or disables the field, and no address availability or key validity is checked.
16: Default contracts are added only on Finish when permitted. The count depends on the network, local IP and existing default peers. The local IP is not its own remote peer.
Show what already exists and what would be added before saving. Explain the predictable-key risk. Disable this option for unsupported configurations instead of pretending all networks can use it.
The fixed counts illustrate 252 possible peers and two existing contracts. The switch does not recalculate the sample counts or write contracts.
17: Successful configuration saving and establishing a VPN connection are separate outcomes. An unconfirmed save belongs to the unknown-result flow, not this success screen.
Offer an explicit choice to connect now or later. A subsequent Android connection may still need system consent and server verification.
The saved message is a prepared scenario. No file was written, and the Connect action does not establish a VPN.
18: A secret mismatch can be associated with the secret field. A transport timeout is a different failure and must not be interpreted as an incorrect secret.
Keep the user on the relevant setup step, preserve editable input and provide a route to correct it. Show HTTP details only when captured data is available.
The mismatch and HTTP example are independent. The sample secret is intentionally fake, and no validation is performed.
19: Contract drafts are tracked by remote IP, including across pages. Keys require 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Changes are saved together and apply on the next connection.
Replace the wide desktop table with a list and detail screens. Retain unsaved edits while navigating. Do not include the local address among remote targets.
Two changed rows and four visible addresses are fixed examples. Save jumps to a confirmed-save scenario. Only two example pages are linked, not all 252 peers.
20: A contract can be enabled or disabled. In the client, a disabled contract has a read-only key, and the password-key action is unavailable. Editing the draft is separate from saving it.

Use a detail screen to avoid a horizontally scrolling table. Explain that both peers need matching keys. Applying a detail should return to the shared draft, not silently commit the whole configuration.
The enable switch changes its appearance only. It does not enforce the actual read-only rule. Apply to draft returns to a fixed list without carrying the entered value.
21: The password-key tool derives a SHA-256 communication key and provides Default and Random actions. It is scoped to the selected contract, not the server secret or access key.
Keep the target IP visible. Show the derived key separately from the password. Applying the key should update only the intended contract draft.
No hashing or random generation is implemented. The shown hash is illustrative and does not correspond to the entered password. Default and Random show explanatory messages.
22: An invalid contract key blocks saving. Validation identifies the first invalid peer, and the required format is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
Attach the error to the affected input, identify the target peer and preserve other draft changes. Provide the password-key route as an alternative way to obtain a valid key.
The six-character example is static. Typing does not update the error, and Back to editing opens a separate prepared page.
23: The full editor retains access to masterSetup, runtime and communicationContracts. The validator checks known fields and their constraints. Saving and resetting are distinct operations.
Preserve the complete document in a scrollable editor. Keep secrets out of incidental status text. Do not assume that Android uses the desktop configuration path.
The sample is not a production configuration. Optional wizard preferences are omitted. Save does not validate or persist edits and opens the saved-while-connected scenario.
24: Reset loads defaults into the editor draft. It must not be presented as an immediate write to the saved configuration. Saving remains a separate action.
Explain which unsaved content will be lost and offer a clear way to keep it. A confirmation here is a proposed mobile presentation of that draft replacement.
Reset in editor opens a schematic default excerpt. It does not modify the live configuration or carry the previous draft forward.
25: Saved changes do not change the existing connection immediately. The desktop offers reconnect after saving, and a new connection must follow completion of the disconnect operation.
Offer reconnect now or use the configuration next time. If VPN is inactive, offer Connect instead. Do not report the new configuration as active before reconnect succeeds.
Reconnect links directly to the connecting sample. The required disconnect phase is not executed. Choosing later returns to a fixed connected sample.
26: The screen contains ten read-only fields: four IPv4 packet/byte counters, three HTTP body-size values and three data-poll counts. HTTP body size is not the same measurement as IPv4 traffic.
Group counters by layer and show their connection context. Do not infer speed, ping or historical charts from cumulative counters alone.
All values and the connection duration are fixed samples. There is no live polling, reset control or historical data store.
27: When status is unavailable after valid data was received, the statistics model retains the last counters and marks them stale. No prior sample is different from zero traffic.
Keep a visible stale-data notice near the values. Do not animate retained values as though they are live. Use the waiting state when no valid sample has ever arrived.
The counters match a prepared previous snapshot. They do not age or refresh automatically.
28: The server view distinguishes online with a valid contract, online with an invalid contract and offline. Online is evaluated within 60 seconds of the server-generated timestamp. The local client is omitted.
Show both presence and contract validity, rather than treating online as permission to communicate. Preserve manual and automatic refresh, and use pagination for longer lists.
Three peers and summary counts are fixed. Auto refresh only toggles visually, and Refresh shows a simulation notice. The raw-data page is a separate sample, not the source of this list.
29: The raw server view is read-only and retains the original field names. The displayed response belongs to a verified server-information result, not an editable configuration document.
Provide a readable, scrollable raw view without rewriting protocol keys. Keep its freshness and error handling aligned with the device view in an implementation.
The JSON is an independent test-fixture-style sample. The synthetic serverVersion is not a released version, and this payload is not the data behind the preceding device list.
30: HTTP diagnostics may contain an incomplete response or incomplete system headers. The displayed size refers to content actually received, not a presumed full response.
Label the response scope and keep it read-only. Keep diagnostics tied to their originating attempt rather than presenting old data as the latest failure.
The HTTP 503 response is illustrative. No packet capture or request is performed, and its relationship to other error examples is not causal.
31: The client may reconstruct a request from available application headers. An unknown HTTP version can be displayed as HTTP/?. Reconstruction is not a complete network capture.
State the data provenance and keep the request separate from the response. Avoid implying that unavailable system headers were observed.
The body placeholder and headers are samples. Nothing is sent, and tabs only navigate between prepared pages.
32: The existing editor and wizard lifecycle distinguish unsaved drafts from saved configuration. Closing a dirty draft requires a decision rather than silently losing it.
Use the same decision pattern for system Back and closing a form. Keep editing must return to the originating form and preserve its draft in a real implementation.
This variant always returns to the URL wizard sample. It is not a working generic back stack, and values are not retained across pages.
33: An unknown save result is not failure or success. The wizard checks a receipt, while the contracts workflow can inspect current configuration. Retry is exposed only when the relevant controller permits it.
Preserve the draft and clearly distinguish inspection from another write. Do not silently overwrite configuration after a service restart or uncertain response.
Verify save opens one prepared contracts outcome. This is not a universal recovery algorithm for the wizard or editor. No receipt or configuration is read.
34: About exists in the desktop menu. The design does not establish a new released client version or licensing terms.
Populate the actual version from the build when implemented. Keep design-package information separate from real product metadata.
Provided by the build is deliberately a placeholder. This screen describes the concept, not an installed Android build.
35: Desktop Exit exists, but it is not the same operation as leaving an Android activity. Mobile activity and VPN service lifecycles are distinct.
Leaving the screen can retain a connection accessible through a notification. Stopping VPN should wait for confirmed disconnection. Do not pretend that closing a screen force-stops the process.
The two choices open notification or disconnecting samples. They do not background an Android app or stop a running service. Always-on behavior is not modeled.
36: The wizard distinguishes unavailable or unusable configuration from a valid draft. Editing is relevant only when the document can be read as supported text. Reset still waits for final saving.
Explain the actual classification rather than showing one generic destructive reset. Offer repair when possible and defaults as a deliberate choice.
This is one generic invalid-document example. The links do not detect missing files, permissions or text encoding, and reset does not read real defaults.
37: The denial belongs to Android permission handling, not the desktop server-verification workflow. It must not be treated as bad credentials.
Leave the configuration intact and offer a deliberate request to try permission again, or remain disconnected. Only the system can grant permission.
Request permission again reopens the illustrative HTML dialog. No operating-system permission state exists in the mockup.
38: The progress UI can report Disconnect not confirmed when a request or status read does not establish completion. The connection may still be active.
Offer another disconnect attempt or a status check without claiming success. Keep the unknown state visible until authoritative status is available.
Both actions navigate to pending examples. No status query is performed and no timeout is simulated.
39: Invalid JSON cannot be accepted as a valid configuration. Actual error detail must come from the parser or validator. Do not promise a line location that the backend does not return.
Keep the document available for correction and preserve edits. Distinguish syntax errors from valid JSON that violates configuration constraints.
The missing separator and error message are fixed. Editing the excerpt does not revalidate it or enable a real save.
40: Wizard reset discards the current setup draft and returns to defaults. It does not commit those defaults before Finish.
State that draft progress will be lost and that the saved configuration remains unchanged. Return to the first setup step after a confirmed reset.
Both choices lead to the prefilled URL example. The demonstration does not load the real default placeholder or preserve previous edits.
41: Contract drafts are retained by target IP across pagination. A save covers the shared draft, not just the visible page.
Preserve the changed-row count while switching pages. Do not lose edits when rows leave the viewport. Keep the local IP out of candidate peers.
This is only the second sample page. It returns to the same fixed detail example for any row and does not implement all 252 addresses.
42: Editor defaults remain a draft until saving. The service supplies the complete default document in the actual client.
Make the unsaved state explicit and provide a route to complete network details. Do not present a schematic excerpt as a ready-to-import configuration.
The displayed JSON is intentionally incomplete. Continue and the wizard link do not transfer edits or reproduce the exact default document.
43: Before any valid service-status sample arrives, the statistics model uses missing-value placeholders. These are not zero counters.
Show a waiting explanation and replace placeholders only when a valid result arrives. Keep this distinct from stale values retained after a later failure.
The dashes remain static. Use the scenario selector to inspect valid data or unavailable status.
44: A valid server response can yield no remote-client rows, because the local client is omitted. An empty list is distinct from a failed or unverifiable response.
Explain the empty result and retain refresh. Do not invent devices or use a connection-error message for a valid empty list.
No response is parsed. Refresh only shows a sample message and does not populate the list.
45: A failed refresh retains the previous successful server information. If no previous valid data exists, the client cannot present a cached list as though it had received one.
Mark the displayed snapshot as stale and keep its refresh time visible. Avoid implying that a last-known online device is online now.
The timestamps and devices are fixed. Retry opens the prepared successful page instead of issuing a request.
46: The contracts workflow exposes Save draft again only when its state permits repetition after checking current configuration. A confirmed prior write should lead to success instead of resubmission.
Distinguish unchanged, already-saved and conflicting results. Do not quietly overwrite a document changed elsewhere. Let the user inspect the current configuration.
This page illustrates only the draft-not-saved branch. It performs no comparison, revision check or conflict resolution.
47: sessionExpired is a separate wizard state. A new session is required before continuing, and obsolete verification results must not authorize a new save.
Explain how to restart setup and offer inspection of current configuration, especially after an uncertain save or service restart.
Reopen wizard navigates to the URL sample. It does not establish a service session or restore a previous draft.
48: These are the four checks shown by connection progress. Successful results describe that connection attempt, not a new independent verification request.
Provide a read-only detail with a clear route back to status. Opening it should not reconnect or reset the connection.
All four checks are fixed as successful. The connecting state in the scenario selector is an alternative example, not an action triggered by viewing details.
